Subject: Q3 capacity ask — Gold tier burst pattern

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Nimble's product and timing look like a good fit. Before we move to an LOI, procurement needs a concrete capacity picture for the "Gold" commit bucket. Two specific asks:

1) For our expected launch bursts (we expect short live events where traffic spikes to ~120K rps of inference calls for ~6–9 minutes), can you translate that into tokens-per-minute estimates and approximate GPUs required?
2) Can you show projected p95/p99 latency under the burst vs steady-state? We have a p99 SLA target of 600ms for the core summarization endpoint.

I'm attaching our traffic sketch; happy to hop on a call.

Best,
Samantha

Samantha — thanks for the sketch. Looping Ben and Marissa for sizing + commercial input. Quick note on approach before we model:

- We'll convert RPS -> tokens/min using your average tokens per request (from the doc: 1,600 tokens/request during summarization bursts).
- We'll model both steady-state and a 9-minute burst window with continuous batching and prefix caching enabled.
- Target p99 <= 600ms for the endpoint. We'll show two knobs: conservative (no burst autoscale) and proactive (reserved slab + short burst headroom).

I've started a working workbook (attached) with an initial tokens/min line and per-GPU tokens/min capacity assumptions based on the Redwood runtime profile for the open-base-quant model. Ben/Marissa — can you validate the per-GPU nominals and the latency multipliers for degraded packing?

—So

On Tue, Mar 29, 2027 at 9:02 AM Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Samantha — thanks for the sketch. Looping Ben and Marissa for sizing + commercial input. Quick note on approach before we model:
>
> - We'll convert RPS -> tokens/min using your average tokens per request (from the doc: 1,600 tokens/request during summarization bursts).
>
> I've started a working workbook (attached) with an initial tokens/min line and per-GPU tokens/min capacity assumptions based on the Redwood runtime profile for the open-base-quant model. Ben/Marissa — can you validate the per-GPU nominals and the latency multipliers for degraded packing?

Soojin / team — validated numbers below based on our latest benchmark matrix on A100-80GB instances with quantized model variant (openbase-q4_0):

- Nominal sustained throughput per GPU (steady small-batch workload): 2,500,000 tokens/min (≈41.6k tokens/sec) at p95 ~180ms, p99 ~320ms.
- Pack-degraded throughput (high-concurrency, less efficient batching during burst): assume 55% of nominal → 1,375,000 tokens/min (≈22.9k tokens/sec). p95 ~260ms, p99 ~520ms.
- Cold-start/scale jitter penalty: add +15% latency at p99 during autoscale events.

Quick calc with your peek: 120K RPS * 1,600 tokens/request = 192,000,000 tokens/min (this number looks large because RPS in your note was request-level; confirm whether 120K RPS was requests/second or tokens/second). If instead the burst is 120K requests/min, that's a different story — please confirm.

Assuming you meant 2,000 requests/sec (i.e., 120K requests/min) producing ~192M tokens/min, at pack-degraded throughput per GPU (1.375M tokens/min): ~140 GPUs to cover burst strictly (no latency oversubscription). With proactive reserved slabs + 20% buffer and autoscale to add 30 GPUs for burst, we can meet p99 <= 600ms in most cases.

Actions: Marissa — can you draft two commercial options: (A) Reserved slab for steady-state (40 GPUs) + burst pool on-demand (up to +140 GPUs), (B) Larger reserved slab (80 GPUs) with smaller on-demand buffer (+80 GPUs) and a discount band for committed tokens/min?

—Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@nimblehealth.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 capacity ask — Gold tier burst pattern

Samantha / team — thanks for the clarifications on the RPS vs RPM ambiguity. We've updated the workbook and attached a short note that walks through the math and proposed commercial structures. Summary here: 

- Clarified peak shape: Nimble confirmed the spike is ~2,000 requests/sec for 7–9 minutes (consistent with Soojin's follow-up). That equates to ~3.2M tokens/sec or ~192M tokens/min during the peak (with 1,600 tokens/req).
- Sizing options (rounded):
  • Option A (conservative): 40 reserved GPUs (handles steady-state + daily peaks) + up to 160 burst GPUs on-demand. Expect average p99 ~420–560ms during burst with our packing heuristics; p95 comfortably <300ms.
  • Option B (aggressive reserve): 100 reserved GPUs + 60 on-demand. Better predictable latency (p99 ~350–480ms) and lower unit cost; suitable if Nimble wants stable monthly billing.
  • Option C (short-term pilot): 20 reserved GPUs + autoscale to 80 on-demand for initial launch. Will likely see p99 near the 600ms SLA during highest peaks; recommend rolling redelivery windows for non-critical jobs.

- Headroom and SLO notes: we model a 25% headroom buffer to avoid hitting degraded packing for transient spikes. If events are larger than 9 minutes or sustained, we'll recommend guardrails (ingress throttles or queuing).

Next steps: We attached "q3_gold_commit_sla_draft.pdf" with proposed SLA language and pricing bands for A/B/C. If Nimble is comfortable, Marissa proposes a quick alignment call Monday to finalize the LOI language.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts – Redwood Inference
